title: AusKidTalk: developing an orthographic annotation workflow for a speech corpus of Australian English-speaking children
why_promising: Primary non-singing Australian-English child production from 620 children aged 3–12 across five elicitation tasks. The Task 1 workflow produced target-word time-aligned Praat TextGrids/CSV with exhaustive human correction or from-scratch transcription for 461 files; manual decisions include labels, boundaries, child/non-child rejection, noise, and phoneme-level discrepancy flags. A 380-file sample involved 85,436 reviewed intervals and 61,371 identified target words. This is highly relevant to clinical/developmental production, categorical error labels, timing, task, age, gender, and group metadata.
open_question: The corpus data are currently available under a data-custodian/on-request model rather than as a public research deposit. Keep in review until a publicly accessible corpus release or authorized data-access endpoint can be identified and exact redistributable annotation/measurement files can be enumerated. Do not ingest code-only outputs or infer unavailable phonetic labels.
